OBSERVED: dispatchDirective() permits an explicit retry from durable status=FAILED only when retry policy is enabled and the stored error/attempt count is authorized.
enqueueDirective() handles that path by awaiting existing.retry() on the failed BullMQ job before dispatchDirective updates the durable DirectiveDispatch row to ENQUEUED.
After existing.retry() resolves, the BullMQ worker can receive the retried job while the durable row is still FAILED.
claimDirectiveDispatch() has no FAILED branch and can only CAS PENDING/ENQUEUED to PROCESSING; a FAILED row therefore falls through to BUSY.
processJob() normalizes BUSY to JobState.CANCELLED with commandResult='Dispatch already processing' and returns successfully.

The retried BullMQ job can therefore complete without executing SWARM, after which dispatchDirective may still write durable status=ENQUEUED, creating a false pending/enqueued projection for a job that was already acknowledged.
EXPECTED: An explicitly authorized retry from FAILED must establish a durable state/order that allows exactly one worker to claim and execute the retried job.
A valid authorized retry must not be dropped as BUSY/CANCELLED solely because BullMQ scheduling outruns the durable FAILED->ENQUEUED projection update.
Failed retry remains bounded by the canonical safe-error allowlist and attempt cap.
Durable projection and BullMQ job state must converge without false ENQUEUED or silent completion.

CRITICAL_INTERLEAVING: D reads durable FAILED row and verifies retry policy.
enqueueDirective awaits existing.retry(); BullMQ makes the failed job runnable.
W receives the job before D persists durable ENQUEUED.
W claim sees FAILED, cannot CAS it, returns BUSY.
W processJob returns CANCELLED successfully and BullMQ completes the retry.
D persists ENQUEUED, leaving durable state ahead of no runnable job.
